Identity.History: The Royal Stoa (Stoa Basileios) stood on the northwest side of the Athenian Agora and was one of the city’s oldest and most important civic buildings. It served as the official seat of the archon basileus, the magistrate responsible for many of Athens’ religious duties and certain sacred legal cases. Though relatively modest in size, the stoa had great symbolic importance, linking the daily political life of the Agora with Athens’ ancient religious traditions.
